sections.What the paper proposes: The paper (The 52-Week High and Momentum Investing) proposes Nearness to the 52-week high: the stock's price at the end of month t-1 divided by its highest price during the 12-month period ending on the last day of month t-1 as the signal, sorted by top_bottom_percent, favoring the winner portfolio: top 30% of stocks with the highest ratio of current price to 52-week high (long leg). Rationale: Traders use the 52-week high as a reference point (anchor) when evaluating news: near the 52-week high they are reluctant to bid prices up as far as good news warrants, and far from it they are reluctant to sell as low as bad news implies; the information eventually prevails, producing continuation (anchoring-and-adjustment bias).
sections.What we implemented and changed: We adapted 4 fields and assumed 3. Adapted: breakpoints (no exchange or size breakpoints in our universe; equal-count sorts of eligible names); disfavored_group (policy: long-only, no short leg); universe_and_filters (policy: our 415-name S&P 500 survivor universe); sample_period (policy: our snapshot sample). Assumed: price_floor set to none; min_history_days set to 252; min_formation_days set to 15. Portfolios were formed in 132 months with 111.7 names on average.
sections.What the backtest found: Over the sample the strategy returned 10.57% a year net of costs, against 12.71% for the equal-weight universe and 13.45% for SPY. Its Sharpe ratio was 0.57 against 0.65 for the equal-weight universe, and its maximum drawdown was -36.0%. The alpha t-statistic was -1.17; it is reported, not used as a gate. Robustness across costs, sub-periods and ranked groups gave a rho of -1.00.
sections.What the simulation and economics found: Across the simulated paths, incremental fee income versus the equal-weight universe fund had a median present value of -$2.1M, with a 5th to 95th percentile range of -$8.0M to $953k. The share of paths with positive NPV after research cost was 15.4%, and 49.4% once the historical excess return is removed. Break-even AUM is not defined; it is reported, not headlined.
